name: conducting-outsider-review
description: "Use when: Review research as an informed non-specialist or cross-disciplinary reader to detect unclear explanations, hidden assumptions, relevance gaps and misleading summaries."

# Conducting Outsider Review

## Procedure
1. State the intended audience and assumed background, artifact version and review purpose. Read the summary/problem statement first, then the necessary supporting sections. Do not pretend the reviewer is a sampled audience member.
2. Restate the problem, why it matters, what was done, what was found and what remains unknown in plain language. Flag any part that cannot be accurately reconstructed from the artifact.
3. Locate unexplained jargon, undefined constructs, missing context, ambiguous visuals, misleading analogies and unsupported practical implications. Quote only enough text to locate each issue.
4. Check whether a reader can distinguish evidence from assumptions, prediction from causation, proposed from completed work and statistical from practical importance. Preserve uncertainty when simplifying language.
5. Ask relevant questions an outside reader would need answered. Test proposed interpretations against the primary report where available; defer specialized validity questions to method/peer review rather than guessing.
6. Suggest concrete wording, ordering or figure/caption changes. Separate comprehension problems from scientific defects and stylistic preferences.

## Deliver
Write `outsider-review.md` with a plain-language restatement, audience assumptions, localized comprehension issues, misleading-inference risks and proposed fixes. Identify which suggestions need specialist verification.

## Boundaries
This review checks accessibility and relevance; it is not a replacement for technical peer review or actual user comprehension testing. Do not remove material caveats merely to make the story more persuasive.
